items.title: Digital Turbine drops sharply after earnings despite sales growth
items.summary: Digital Turbine shares fell sharply after hours despite strong reported revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth. Rising revenue-sharing costs cut non-GAAP gross margin, and management disclosed a prior-period expense correction assessed as immaterial. The selloff highlights uncertainty over partner economics and durable cash conversion.

items.title: Quantum rises on strong data-storage sales and record backlog
items.summary: Quantum reported rapid revenue growth, margin expansion, near-record order momentum and a major hyperscale storage commitment. Shares rose strongly after hours. A large reported GAAP loss was predominantly affected by a noncash warrant revaluation, so backlog conversion, storage supply and recurring profitability remain central tests.

items.title: AAON posts major data-center cooling growth but identifies material control weakness
items.summary: AAON reported Q3 revenue up 84.1% and BASX data-center-linked sales up 218.3%, with total backlog up 40.5% year over year. The company raised 2026 guidance but restated its first two quarters and disclosed a material weakness in financial controls. Strong conversion and reporting reliability must both be assessed.

items.title: Trade Desk rallies after outlook beat despite ongoing revenue contraction
items.summary: Trade Desk's Q3 revenue slipped 0.5% year over year to $736 million while adjusted earnings beat estimates. Management projects at least $755 million in Q4 revenue and increased available share-repurchase authorization to $1 billion. A sharp extended-hours rebound follows steep 2026 losses, but customer retention and sustained organic growth remain unproven.

items.title: Brent settles down 5.85% at 10-week low despite continuing Hormuz vessel risk
items.summary: Brent settled November 9 at $92.57, down 5.85%, and WTI at $86.85, down 4.38%, extending the earlier intraday retreat. U.S. comments lowered expectations of renewed Iran strikes even as maritime attacks remain a risk. Physical Dated Brent weakness suggests reduced near-term tightness; no newly verified normal transit or additional production interruption was established.
